sources.supports: OpenClaw's own guide presents this plugin for Fastmail, iCloud and similar mailboxes and takes only a mailbox password, with no Google sign-in option.

name: Lost or stolen phone: lock one person out
reason: Locking one person out is a second phrase on the same stop plugin as the kill switch (G005): same hooks, same wave, and this item already lists G005 as what it extends. One combined item covers both; nothing is lost.

sources.title: Plugin hooks: message hooks
sources.supports: Both the stop phrase and the lock-out phrase are claimed by the same plugin hook before the model sees the message, so they are one piece of code.

sources.title: Operator incident response: contain
sources.supports: OpenClaw's incident guide treats stopping the gateway and freezing who may message it as one containment step list.

name: Guest tier: a grandparent or sitter can text Happy and gets a fridge-level card only
reason: A sitter or visiting grandparent would be a lower-trust user on the parents' gateway: OpenClaw's security guidance says mixed-trust use belongs on a separate gateway, and on iMessage everyone admitted to chat is also on the list that may answer approval prompts. The record itself says most sitters will just text the parents, and a sitter is outside the 'messages go only to the family' rule; the sitter sheet (F036), translated when needed (G011) and forwarded by a parent, gives the same card. No other item depends on this one.

sources.title: Gateway security: one trust boundary per gateway
sources.supports: OpenClaw's guidance for people of different trust levels is to split them onto a separate gateway and credentials, not to share one.

sources.title: iMessage rich messages: approvals
sources.supports: On iMessage the admission list is also the approver list, so a guest who is let in to chat is also authorised to answer approval prompts.

name: Standing orders: a written charter per recurring job
reason: The charter for each job is rendered by the same generator, from the same family.json5 entries, as the jobs registry (G003), which this item names as its dependency. It is one piece of wave-A work, so it becomes part of G003. No item outside this group depends on it.

sources.title: Standing orders: how they work
sources.supports: OpenClaw describes the written program and the scheduled automation that fires it as one arrangement, which is what the registry generates.

name: Unattended-job guardrails (failure alerts, auto-disable, missed runs)
reason: By its own description this is the set of scheduler settings the jobs registry (G003) should be built on: a time limit and tool cap on every job the registry emits, plus three gateway switches. It is the same piece of wave-A work, so it becomes part of G003. AUT-01 and AUT-03 refer to it for the 'triggers off before any agent gets the automations tool' rule, which moves with it.

sources.title: openclaw automations: timeouts
sources.supports: The per-job time limit is a flag on the same add and edit command the registry generator emits, so the guardrail is part of generating the job.

sources.title: Automation delivery: failure notifications
sources.supports: Failure alerts are a built-in scheduler policy that only needs routing to the operator, a config line set once alongside the registry.

name: Per-person and per-agent spend caps with a daily cost line
reason: The caps and the alert already exist: every OpenAI project has a hard monthly limit and a Grafana rule alerts Tony when an agent passes its daily budget (happy-config baseline/caps-m1.md, confirmed 9 Oct). What is left is a rule, 'every new agent or key gets its own cap and budget line before it goes live', which is a line on the operator's checklist (OCL-13), not a feature. VOX-02 lists this item as a dependency and OCL-06, OCL-13 and CRT-04 mention it; they should point at that checklist line.

sources.title: OpenAI API guide: Spend limits
sources.supports: The hard stop is a setting on each OpenAI project, made once in the provider's dashboard; there is nothing for Happy to build.

sources.title: Prometheus metrics
sources.supports: The per-agent cost counter that the existing daily-budget alert reads is exported by the Gateway already.

name: Nightly backups and a quarterly restore drill
reason: Already running since M0: a verified archive of Happy's state every night at 03:15, 14 days kept, on the encrypted disk and in the encrypted Time Machine backup, and one restore drill passed. What is left is the roadmap's standing rule to repeat the drill each quarter and to add new stores to the backup set, which are lines on the operator's checklist (OCL-13), not a feature. CRT-05 lists 'G007 backups' as a dependency, which is already met; OCL-10 and OCL-13 only mention it.

sources.title: Backup CLI
sources.supports: The archive-and-verify step is one built-in command, which the existing nightly script already runs; nothing further has to be built.

sources.title: Apple Support: Back up your Mac with Time Machine
sources.supports: The encrypted off-disk copy is a macOS feature that is already switched on for this Mac.

name: Apple Foundation Models as the free on-device utility model
reason: Its own description says the family sees no difference: the Apple on-device model only writes session titles and progress notes on screens Happy does not use. The one use the catalog kept it for, a free local classifier behind the privacy gate, is not documented for it, and OCL-14 now covers local classification by a documented route. No other item depends on it.

sources.title: Agent model configuration
sources.supports: The utility model powers Control UI session titles, activity recaps and progress narration, none of which appear in an iMessage thread.

sources.title: Decision models: roles
sources.supports: Classification is the documented job of the decision-model role, which OCL-14 fills with a local provider.

name: Weekday morning brief (07:00, no mail yet)
reason: This is the same job as the evening brief on a different schedule: the same calendar and weather, the same tools, built in the same piece of work. It becomes the optional 07:00 schedule of the combined briefs entry (F014).

sources.title: Keep the Family Up to Date with Daily Agenda Emails | Cozi Family Organizer
sources.supports: Cozi sends family members a morning email of the day's calendar events and offers the weekly agenda as a second setting of the same feature, which is how the combined briefs entry now treats them.

sources.title: CLI reference: automations (cron)
sources.supports: Each brief is one scheduled agent job created from a cron line, so the morning, evening and Sunday briefs differ only in schedule and prompt.

name: Sunday 18:00 week-ahead
reason: This is the same job as the evening brief with a Sunday schedule and a seven-day window: the same calendar and weather, the same tools, built in the same piece of work. It becomes the Sunday 18:00 schedule of the combined briefs entry (F014).

sources.title: Wish You Had an Instant Way To Tell Everyone the Family’s Weekly Plan? (Cozi blog)
sources.supports: Cozi's weekly agenda email goes to chosen family members on Sundays with the week's events, a second schedule of the same agenda feature as its daily email.

sources.title: Automation schedules
sources.supports: A brief's schedule is one cron expression in a named time zone, so the Sunday week-ahead is the evening brief's job with a different line.

name: Overnight interest brief on the research agent
reason: The entry itself says to skip it if a parent uses Gemini or Google Alerts, and Gemini already does daily topic tracking for up to ten topics. The catalog had already dropped this kind of topic brief once, and its one example (a registration date opening) is the page watcher's job (F029).

sources.title: Schedule actions in Gemini Apps - Gemini Apps Help
sources.supports: Gemini already offers daily topic tracking and news digests as scheduled actions, up to ten at a time, with or without a paid Google AI plan.

name: Family week board in the Control UI (pinned native report)
reason: The board lives in OpenClaw's Control UI, which the vendor calls an admin surface, so in practice only Tony could open it, and it cannot be shown in iMessage. The entry itself says the phones' calendar widgets and the evening and Sunday briefs already cover it; four earlier board entries (AUT-10, HOM-10, MKT-09, MAC-08) were removed for the same reasons.

sources.title: Dashboard (Control UI) access and auth
sources.supports: The vendor describes the Control UI, where the board would live, as an admin surface for chat, config and approvals, not a page to hand to the rest of the family.

sources.title: Show widget: availability
sources.supports: Channel runs such as iMessage are not offered the widget tool, so the board can never be asked for or shown in the family's thread.

name: Week sheet on paper as a no-model job
reason: This is the Sunday fridge sheet that the printing entry (F080) already lists. The only thing it adds is a build detail: producing the sheet with a plain scheduled script and no model call.

sources.title: Automation payloads: command payloads
sources.supports: A scheduled command can run a script with no model call; that is the one thing this entry adds, and it is a build choice for the fridge sheet F080 already includes.

name: Urgent school alert relay (snow day, delay, early dismissal, bus, safety)
reason: The school's own alert system already sends closures and delays straight to both parents' phones and cannot be muted, so Happy's relay would arrive second, and a wrong 'routine' label could hide a closure. The one useful rule (do not hold an urgent school email until 16:00) moves into the school digest (F056); OCL-14 names this relay as a user of its classifier and SRC-08 calls it a backup, so both should point to F056.

sources.title: ParentSquare: Help Please! Frequently Asked Parent Questions
sources.supports: A widely used school messaging vendor says urgent alerts and attendance notices always come through whatever the parent's notification setting, and that only the school can stop them.

name: School platform feed map: what each system really sends
reason: This is a setup recipe and a record of what each school system sends, not something Happy does by itself: a parent sets each platform's notification options once and the result shows up only inside the school digest. It moves into that entry (F056) as its per-platform setup. No other entry depends on it; the line another review folds in here (IPH-15) travels with it.

sources.title: PowerSchool SIS student and parent help: Email Notifications
sources.supports: What this entry describes is a parent filling in the platform's own notification settings once, including an extra recipient address, which is a setup step for the school mailbox and its digest.

sources.title: ParentSquare: Help Please! Frequently Asked Parent Questions
sources.supports: ParentSquare's evening Digest is a setting the parent chooses per school, again a one-time configuration and not an agent feature.

name: Google Classroom guardian summaries in the school digest
reason: A Classroom guardian summary is one more email arriving in the school mailbox, and its whole result is one line inside the school digest, the same way the lunch-balance and library notices were handled earlier. It becomes a sender in F056 instead of a separate entry; it also only applies if the school uses Google Classroom, which nobody has checked.

sources.title: Get Classroom email summaries (for guardians) - Classroom Help
sources.supports: The guardian summary is an ordinary email that can go to any address, so in the school mailbox it is one more school message for the existing digest to read.

name: School lunch menu answers (no documented feed)
reason: There is no documented menu feed to watch, and the menu vendor's own site and app already show the current menu, while a once-a-month import would sometimes be wrong and Happy must never be the allergy authority. If a parent does send the monthly menu, that is ordinary snap-to-action (F011) and needs no entry of its own; the lunch-balance line already lives in the school digest (F056).

sources.title: Nutrislice: K-12 school foodservice solutions
sources.supports: The menu vendor already puts each school's menu online and on phones for parents, and its product page mentions no feed, API or calendar subscription a home agent could read.

sources.title: Web fetch
sources.supports: Happy's page reader does not run JavaScript, so a script-rendered menu page would return no menu to it.

name: Practice drills: spelling lists, math facts, reading buddy and bedtime story
reason: The parent-run drills are the same thing as the practice quiz in MKT-02 with a typed list in place of a photo, and the entry itself says a parent can already run them from their own chat. The version the kids would use themselves cannot exist before the kids agent (F072), and 'reading buddy' and 'bedtime story' were named but never described.

sources.title: Introducing Alexa+, the next generation of Alexa
sources.supports: The products that ship this treat it as one function, a quiz made from whatever material the user supplies, so a typed spelling list and a photographed study guide are the same feature.

sources.title: Session management
sources.supports: The running score is just conversation state that lasts until the daily reset, so the drills need nothing built beyond the quiz prompt.

name: Kid-safe weekly card baked into the kids agent
reason: The printed Sunday fridge sheet already shows the kids the week's schedule and chore turns, the paediatricians' advice is a chart posted where the child sees it, and the product that sells this to families is a wall display, not a chat for children. A chat version would also put the family's weekly schedule into the kids agent, which the roadmap describes as holding nothing to steal, and it needs a calendar reader and a notes store that do not exist. Nothing depends on it (OCL-03 and HOM-14 only list it as an overlap).

sources.title: Age-Appropriate Chores for Children - HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics)
sources.supports: The paediatricians' guidance is a chore list posted in the child's room or on the refrigerator, which the printed week sheet provides without a chat agent.

sources.title: Skylight Calendar | Smart Family Calendar
sources.supports: The product that sells this to families does it as a shared family display showing each person's events and chores, not as a chat agent for children.

name: Kid check-in relay and kid-side chore done
reason: A child who has an Apple account to text Happy can text a parent or the family chat directly, the iPhone's own Check In can tell a parent automatically when the child's phone has arrived, and Family Sharing shows the device in Find My. The record itself says no source shows kids would text the agent instead of a parent. Nothing else depends on it (CRT-03 only borrowed the hook shape).

sources.title: Use Check In for Messages on iPhone (Apple Support)
sources.supports: The iPhone's Messages app can tell a chosen person automatically that the phone has arrived, which is the 'I'm home' relay without an agent in the middle.

sources.title: Family Sharing - Apple
sources.supports: Family Sharing members can share their location and show their devices in Find My, so a parent can already see whether a child's device is at home.

sources.title: Create an Apple Account for your child
sources.supports: A parent creates the child's own Apple Account, the same step that would give the child a handle to text Happy in the first place.

name: Birthday, anniversary and gift-date heads-up
reason: The phones already do the core of this: birthdays saved in contacts appear in the calendar by themselves, and the iPhone calendar can alert up to a week ahead. What is left (anniversary and gift dates with last year's gift note) is a few more rows in the dated-reminders list (F063), not a separate daily job with its own hand-entered table. Nothing depends on it.

sources.title: Manage birthdays on your calendar (Google Calendar Help)
sources.supports: Birthdays saved in Google Contacts show up in the person's Google Calendar automatically, with nothing to enter twice.

sources.title: How to Change the Default Reminder Time in Calendar (iPhone Life)
sources.supports: The iPhone Calendar has a default alert for birthdays that can be set to the day itself, one or two days before, or one week before.

name: Pending items view: approvals waiting, drafts unsent, watchers, reminders, open requests
reason: Once the parts that cannot work are taken out (gateway approvals lapse within ten minutes, and unsent drafts belong to the later mail work), what is left today is the list of scheduled reminders, which the reminders entry (F007) already promises; page watchers would show up in that same list. Open requests and proposals awaiting a yes would need tables that do not exist. Nothing depends on it (OCL-06 and CRT-01 only mention it as an overlap).

sources.title: Manage automations
sources.supports: The same automations list that F007 uses to list reminders returns every scheduled job with its name and next run time, which is the working core of a what-is-pending answer.

sources.title: Plugin permission requests
sources.supports: Approval requests expire after ten minutes at most, so there is no day-long queue of waiting approvals to show.

name: Fact check and official-source answers
reason: A fact check is the research helper answering under the citation and freshness rules (F022); the record's own build note says its rubric is folded into the F022 section, so there is nothing separate to build. Nothing depends on it.

sources.title: Web fetch: limits and safety
sources.supports: Config offers only a hostname denylist, so 'official sites only' is not a setting; the fact check adds no mechanism beyond the search, fetch and citation rules the research entries already hold.

name: Find a place and route errands: open-now dinner, urgent care, pharmacy, Saturday loop
reason: This is the Places lookup (F021) with an answer format: the same Google Places search, the same open-now and rating filters, the same Maps link. The record also concedes that phone maps apps already answer these questions with live traffic, so it does not earn a separate entry; nothing depends on it.

sources.title: Bundled goplaces skill
sources.supports: The open-now and minimum-rating search this entry describes is the same bundled Places command that F021 wraps.

name: Feed watch for school, PTA, town and library sites (RSS/Atom)
reason: This is the same job as the page watcher (F029): tell the parents when a public school, town or library site posts something new. F029 already says to use a site's own feed first, so the two are one piece of work in the same wave; no other item depends on this one.

sources.title: Bundled skill: blogwatcher
sources.supports: The feed tool this item is built on is the same one already cited on the page watcher, whose order of preference starts with a site's own feed.

sources.title: Automation payloads
sources.supports: Both watchers come down to one scheduled host command with no model in it, so they are one script and one job pattern.

name: Grocery and errand capture by text or voice, plus Saturday shop list
reason: Texting 'add oat milk' is exactly what the shared Reminders bridge (F030) does, and the item's own Apple source says the iPhone already sorts a grocery list by itself. Only the Saturday list text is new, and it fits as one optional job under F030; WEB-11, MKT-05 and SRC-04 use the grocery list and should point to F030.

sources.title: Create grocery lists in Reminders on your iPhone - Apple Support
sources.supports: The iPhone's Reminders app already keeps a grocery list and sorts it into store sections, so capture and sorting need nothing beyond the list bridge.

name: Draft-only outreach texts (vendors, coaches, carpool parents)
reason: Asking Happy to word a text to the plumber or the coach is ordinary chat that works today with nothing to build; what the item really records is the rule that Happy never sends to anyone outside the family, which the family delivery item (G009) already states. CRT-10 mentions it for a draft absence note, which still works without this item.

sources.title: Tool policy (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The only mechanism on the item is that the parent's agent is not granted the send tool, which is the family-only rule and not a feature of its own.

name: Kids' chore rota and after-school routine board (parent-run)
reason: The kids are not users, so this board would only text the parents, and the item itself says a paper chart on the fridge may be less effort. The paediatricians' advice it cites is exactly that, a chore list posted in the child's room or on the refrigerator, which the Sunday fridge sheet (F080) can print; only OCL-03 mentions this entry, as an overlap.

sources.title: Age-Appropriate Chores for Children - HealthyChildren.org (American Academy of Pediatrics)
sources.supports: The paediatricians' advice is a star chart or chore list posted where the child sees it, in their room or on the refrigerator; that is a sheet of paper, not texts to a parent.

name: Document vault: 'file this' (insurance, warranties, manuals)
reason: The parts a parent would notice are already elsewhere: the reminder before a policy or warranty expires is the renewals program (F063), the short summary is a page in the family vault (F043), and appliance manuals belong to the home registry (F034). What is left is a new tool to copy the PDF onto the Mac, while the paperwork kit (CRT-12) already keeps scans in the phone's Files; OCL-08 and CRT-12 mention this entry only as an overlap.

sources.title: openclaw wiki CLI reference (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The vault cannot hold the PDF itself, only a text summary, so everything except a new file-copy tool is already covered by the vault and the renewals list.

name: 'Did I get an email about X?' lookup and thread summary
reason: This is what the read-only Gmail connection (F047) is for: a parent asks 'did the dentist confirm?' and their mail agent searches their own inbox, in the same wave and the same piece of work. It becomes F047's example instead of a second item; the thread-summary half is free inside Gmail now, and no other item depends on this one.

sources.title: Bundled gog skill
sources.supports: The lookup uses only the Gmail search and read commands that the read-only connection already gives the owner's mail agent.

sources.title: Gmail is entering the Gemini era (Google, January 2026)
sources.supports: Google says conversation summaries of long email threads are free for every Gmail user, while asking the whole inbox a question needs a paid plan; so the lookup is the part worth keeping, and it is F047.

name: Draft a reply or note (lands in Gmail Drafts)
reason: Gmail now writes reply drafts by itself at no cost, inside the thread the owner must open anyway to press send, and Happy's version would need a Google token that is able to send; the catalog's earlier round already said to leave personal reply drafts to Gmail. It is the Gmail drafts connection (F048) described a second time, so it goes the same way, and the morning digest (F016) should not point here for drafts.

sources.title: Gmail is entering the Gemini era (Google, January 2026)
sources.supports: Google says Help Me Write and Suggested Replies, which draft a reply inside the thread, are rolling out free to every Gmail user: the job this item would do.

sources.title: Gmail API: Choose scopes
sources.supports: The permission that lets an agent write a draft is the same one that lets it send, so Happy's version needs a token that could always send mail.

sources.title: gogcli command reference: gog gmail drafts reply
sources.anchor: Save a reply as a draft
sources.supports: The reply draft would be made by the same gog drafts commands that F048 wraps, so there is no separate mechanism here.

name: Appointment, refill, results and travel-change emails to .ics, reminders and alerts
reason: Each part repeats something the parent's phone already does: Google Calendar adds flights, reservations and ticketed or medical events from Gmail by itself, Apple Calendar suggests events it finds in Mail, and the pharmacy, clinic and airline emails are themselves the alerts. Happy's version would put a watcher on a private inbox, health mail included, to send them a second time; its absorbed bill-due line stays with the morning mail digest (F016), and CRT-10 and CRT-14 mention this entry only as an overlap.

sources.title: Manage your events from Gmail - Google Calendar Help
sources.supports: Google Calendar already adds events from Gmail automatically: flights and other travel, hotel and restaurant reservations, and ticketed or registered events including medical ones.

sources.title: Apple Support: Use Siri Suggestions in Calendar on Mac
sources.supports: Apple's Calendar already picks up events it recognises in Mail and offers them as suggestions.

name: Vehicle recall check by make, model and year (NHTSA)
reason: NHTSA's own free SaferCar app already sends recall alerts for the exact car by its VIN, and for car seats and tires, while Happy's version can only match make, model and year and still has to send the parent off to a VIN check. Nothing else in the catalog depends on this entry.

sources.title: SaferCar on the App Store (developer: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration)
sources.supports: NHTSA's own app takes each vehicle's VIN, plus equipment such as tires and car seats, and notifies the owner of safety recalls on exactly those items.

sources.title: NHTSA's New SaferCar App Aims to Stop Deadly Recall Notification Delays (Consumer Reports)
sources.supports: A recall often covers only some trims or build periods, so an alert tied to the VIN is more accurate than one tied to make, model and year.

sources.title: NHTSA recalls API, live response
sources.supports: The public interface Happy would poll answers by make, model and model year only, so it lists every campaign for the model and cannot say whether this car is affected.

name: Explain this EOB or medical bill
reason: This is the general 'Explain this' feature (F023) pointed at one kind of document: the same photo or PDF in, the same five-line answer out, and nothing extra to build. The medical-bill wording moves into F023. Nothing else depends on this entry.

sources.title: Media understanding
sources.supports: A medical bill arrives through the same generic path as any other attached document, as extracted text wrapped for the reply model, with no bill-specific mechanism.

sources.title: How to read a health insurance explanation of benefits
sources.supports: The federal guide lists the fixed fields an Explanation of Benefits carries, which is all the line template carried into F023 needs.

name: School, camp and sports health-form helper
reason: The enrolment and camp paperwork kit (CRT-12) already promises the copy-paste answers for these forms and names this entry as the piece that supplies them, so the helper is folded into the kit instead of standing alone. Its four sources only show that attachments and prompts work, not a separate family need.

sources.title: Media understanding
sources.supports: A form photo or PDF reaches the model through the ordinary attachment path, so the helper is a prompt template over stored facts and not a separate capability.

name: Pet care program
reason: Nothing here is new work: a monthly dose reminder is an ordinary recurring reminder (F007), vaccine due dates are rows in the renewals look-ahead (F063), and the vet's number belongs in the provider registry (F034). The entry also admits no pet is mentioned in the household. Nothing else depends on it.

sources.title: Automation schedules
sources.supports: The monthly pet reminder is a plain recurring scheduled job, the same mechanism the timed-reminders feature already uses.

sources.title: Keep the Worms Out of Your Pet's Heart! The Facts about Heartworm Disease
sources.supports: Heartworm preventives are given monthly all year with a yearly test, which is one recurring reminder and one dated row, not a separate feature.

name: Spend summary from statements (read-only, local model)
reason: The entry itself questions whether dropping in monthly statements is worth it when bank and card apps already sort spending, and a card issuer's own assistant does send spending summaries and recurring-charge alerts straight from the live account. The wait for a local model is not the reason for removal. Nothing else depends on this entry.

sources.title: Eno, your Capital One assistant | Capital One
sources.supports: A card issuer's own assistant sends cardholders spending insights and summaries and flags items such as free trials and recurring charges, straight from the live account.

name: Computer-control substrate: OpenClaw.app as the Mac node
reason: Installing the OpenClaw Mac app gives the family nothing by itself; it is the first setup step of the screen-control pilot, so it is folded into that one entry (MAC-02). MAC-02, MAC-03, MAC-05 and MAC-07 list it as a dependency; MAC-03 should point to MAC-02 instead.

sources.title: Computer use: Requirements
sources.supports: A paired node that advertises the screenshot and input commands is listed as a requirement of the computer tool, which makes the app install a setup step of screen control and not a capability of its own.

name: Watch Happy work: Screen Sharing and the Control UI Desktop panel
reason: Watching the desk over Screen Sharing is a setup step of the screen-control pilot, and the entry itself says it has no value to the family on its own; it is folded into the pilot (MAC-02). Nothing else depends on it.

sources.title: Computer use
sources.anchor: not ordinary Gateway or paired-node desktops
sources.supports: The built-in pause when a person takes control exists only for cloud desktops, so on a paired Mac the watching view is an aid to a pilot run and not a control or feature of its own.

name: Computer-use acceptance test: ten household tasks before any go-live
reason: This is the pass-or-fail test for the screen-control pilot, not something the family uses, and it cannot run until the pilot's other pieces exist; it becomes the pilot's go-live gate inside MAC-02. MAC-07 lists it as a dependency and is removed in the same round.

sources.title: Computer use: Requirements
sources.supports: The computer tool needs a paired node, a vision model and a tool-policy grant before it runs at all, so a test of it can only be built as part of the same pilot work.

name: Operate one Mac app that has no API (pilot: fill a flat PDF form)
reason: The entry itself says Preview on a parent's Mac already fills and signs these forms with no agent and that a parent is usually faster by hand, while the screen-control route would send a child's health and insurance details to a cloud model as screenshots. The useful part, ready-to-paste answers for a form, is already F067.

sources.title: Fill out and sign PDF forms in Preview on Mac (Apple Support)
sources.supports: Apple's own Preview app fills PDF forms, offers a text box for forms that will not accept typing and adds a signature, so the same job is done on a parent's Mac with no agent.

sources.title: Computer use tool: Limitations (Anthropic)
sources.supports: A model vendor tells developers not to use computer use for tasks that need perfect precision or involve sensitive user information without human oversight; placing text on a scanned form of a child's health details is both.

sources.title: Computer use guide (OpenAI)
sources.supports: The family's model vendor treats typing sensitive information into a form as sending data out, an action a person is expected to confirm.

name: Phone-node command ceiling: deny first, then pair
reason: This is the 'deny first' step of pairing a phone, and the pairing entries already repeat nearly all of it (limited setup codes, Gateway-wide allow and deny lists, keeping agents away from the phone). It becomes step 1 of the single iPhone-app entry (OCL-01); nothing else depends on it, and with no phone paired today nothing is left unguarded in the meantime.

sources.title: Node command policy
sources.supports: One Gateway-wide deny list overrides every platform default and allow entry, so the phone ceiling is the same config list that MAC-04 and the pairing entry already edit.

sources.title: Node command policy
sources.supports: The setting that makes the Gateway ignore tools published by paired phones is the same one OCL-01 already tells the operator to set.

name: Pair an iPhone as an OpenClaw node (official iOS app)
reason: Pairing the iPhone app and using the iPhone app are one install and one setup code on the same phone, and OCL-01 already describes that pairing, so they are kept as one entry under OCL-01. IPH-02 and IPH-04 list this as a dependency and VOX-01 needs the same pairing; they should point to OCL-01, and IPH-02 keeps its own spare-phone notes if it survives.

sources.title: openclaw qr: Setup code contents
sources.supports: One setup code issues the phone's node token and its operator chat session together, so pairing the node and getting the chat app are a single step.

sources.title: iOS app: What it does
sources.supports: The same official app is described as both the device node and the chat surface, which is why the two entries describe one install.

name: Read a parent's calendar, reminders, contacts and step count from their phone

sources.title: Sonos - Home Assistant
sources.supports: Home Assistant's Sonos integration plays an announcement over the music and restores the volume, and needs TCP port 1443 on each speaker; this is the one thing the hub route adds, and it is carried into F076. Opened in this run.

sources.title: Install Home Assistant on macOS
sources.supports: On a Mac the hub means an always-on virtual machine (2 GB RAM, 2 vCPUs), and the page sends people not familiar with virtual machines to a dedicated board; that cost is why it stays a later option. Opened in this run.

name: Camera snapshot on request (did the package come?)
reason: The entry's own note says a video doorbell's app already sends package alerts with nothing to build, and that Happy's version is worth building only for a camera with a local stream and no such alerts. Round 2 added that note without testing the 'only if': a doorbell that has the local stream this entry waits for also lists package detection and instant phone alerts, so the maker's app answers 'did the package come?' first, without sending porch pictures that may show the kids to a cloud model. The house owns no such camera, and nothing else depends on this entry.

sources.title: Reolink Video Doorbell PoE (maker's product page)
sources.supports: A doorbell camera that lists RTSP and ONVIF among its protocols, the local stream this entry needs, also lists package detection and an instant push notification to the phone, with no monthly fees for local storage, so the maker's app already does the job. Opened in this run.

sources.title: Learn about package alerts - Google Home and Nest Help
sources.supports: Google's doorbells send a notification to the phone when a package is detected, with no subscription needed on three current Nest models; this is the page the entry's own caveat leans on. Opened in this run.

sources.title: steipete/camsnap
sources.supports: The tool Happy's version would wrap keeps camera passwords in a plain-text config file, a cost the maker's app does not add (already on the entry, checked ok).

name: Local classifier calls (decision_evaluate with an on-device ONNX model)
reason: Folded, not dropped: by its own words this is a building block that no card needs yet, and nothing lists it as a dependency. Rounds 2 and 3 kept it for three later uses without testing them: the school digest (F051) has no hook that would call it, the roadmap's kids filters are Llama Guard 3 and Prompt Guard 2, which are not on this plugin's model list, and the privacy gate (F002) already carries the one line saying a local classifier could later replace its pattern match.

sources.title: Local ONNX decision models: model list
sources.supports: The plugin runs a fixed list of seven general-purpose classifier models; neither of the kids filters the roadmap chose is among them.

sources.title: Decision models (OpenClaw docs)
sources.supports: The installed docs still describe both decision-model plugins as unpublished candidates, and say elsewhere on the page that no automatic consumer is connected.

name: Family-only delivery: text the other parent or the parents' group, and ask-and-relay a yes or no, with the recipient pinned in code
reason: Happy will not text one parent from the other parent's chat or carry a question and a yes or no between the two of you; Tony approved leaving that off on 12 Oct, as the roadmap and today's settings have it. 'Tell Jordan...', or a note for anyone outside the family, keeps getting a draft you send yourself, and anything meant for both parents is two scheduled texts, one each, or the group chat once that card is built.

sources.title: Configuration — tool policy
sources.supports: The message tool is the single member of group:messaging, so it is granted or denied as one unit.

sources.title: Tool and agent permissions
sources.supports: The documented built-in limits on where the message tool may send are switches for other conversations, open by default; nothing on the page pins recipients, so a hook is needed.

sources.title: Hook reference
sources.supports: A before_tool_call handler that throws or times out blocks the tool call, so a recipient check placed there cannot be skipped by an error.

sources.title: Agent send
sources.supports: A host-side script can run one agent turn and deliver the reply to a chat target from the command line.

name: When the model is down: an honest notice, jobs that need no model, and an optional same-vendor fallback
reason: Tony approved dropping the outage script (S14): a parent who texts during an outage already sees Happy's own error line, and Tony already gets the model and gateway alerts on his phone. The fixed reminders rebuilt as no-model jobs go too, and the fallback to the vendor's smaller model stays off as it is today, so nothing of this card is left to build.

sources.title: Model failover: selection source policy
sources.supports: An agent's own primary model is strict unless that agent's model object lists fallbacks; an empty list makes strictness explicit.

sources.title: openclaw automations: command jobs
sources.supports: A scheduled job can run a fixed command and deliver its output with no model call.

sources.title: openclaw models status --check: exit codes
sources.supports: A clean status check covers auth and routing only and is explicitly not proof that a model request will succeed.

sources.title: OpenAI Status: incident history
sources.supports: The vendor's own history page lists dozens of incidents a month in autumn 2026, including API-wide error-rate incidents.

name: Notification policy: daily cap, quiet hours, priority classes and job tags, plus snooze, mute and vacation mode by chat
reason: Tony approved dropping the notification-policy plugin (S4): no daily cap, no enforced quiet hours, no urgent or not-urgent split, and no 'mute until 3' or holiday pause by chat. He never asked for a cap or quiet hours, and a text that such a plugin cancels is logged as a failed delivery, which is why other cards carried workarounds for it.

sources.title: Message and delivery hooks (installed docs)
sources.supports: A plugin can rewrite or cancel any outgoing message just before delivery.

sources.title: Hook reference (installed docs)
sources.anchor: Log and skip the failed handler
sources.supports: Outbound delivery hooks are not hard gates: if the handler throws or times out the message is still sent.

sources.title: Outbound delivery preparation (installed source)
sources.supports: The shared outbound stage runs the reply-payload hook only when the caller passes a hook descriptor, while message_sending runs whenever a handler is registered.

sources.title: Scheduler announce delivery (installed source)
sources.supports: Scheduled announce deliveries are sent through the durable batch call without a reply-payload hook descriptor.

name: Renewals, expiry and upkeep look-ahead (passports, licences, car, domains, filed documents, check-ups, home and car upkeep)
reason: Each renewal, expiry or upkeep date becomes one event with an alert on the family's shared calendar, typed once by a parent, which also works when Happy is down. That leaves no dates table, no monthly script and no 'coming due' text to build.

sources.title: Automation payloads
sources.supports: An empty tool allowlist switches off every agent tool for the job, so the renewal table has to be in the prompt or bootstrap text rather than looked up at run time.

sources.title: User model
sources.supports: Cron sessions do not get MEMORY.md injected, so the table cannot live only in the memory vault.

sources.title: Renew an adult passport
sources.supports: Some countries and airlines refuse entry when a passport has under six months left, which is why the passport reminder needs a long lead time.

sources.title: Get a passport for a minor under 18
sources.supports: Passports for children under 16 last five years and cannot be renewed; the child must apply again in person with a parent.
